app.name: bexio API app (own OAuth app for Composio custom auth)

verdict.summary: Composio has no managed OAuth app for bexio, so you must register your own app at developer.bexio.com and paste its client ID and secret into Composio. The registration itself is quick, but the exact redirect URL must match, and the docs do not say whether apps need review before other companies can connect.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for your own connection; add more time for scope trimming and any Marketplace listing
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30-60 minutes once you have a bexio account
verdict.approval_wait: None documented for creating an OAuth app. Marketplace listing timing is not published and is at bexio's discretion.

gates.name: Own app, own account (developer access)
gates.unlocks: Create the app at developer.bexio.com, reveal client credentials, and connect your own bexio account through Composio.
limits: Requires a bexio account; the docs suggest a trial account at bexio.com if you have none.
Access runs with the user rights of the person who set up the connection.
Redirect URLs must be registered in advance; unknown URLs are refused at authorization.

gates.name: No documented invited-user tier
gates.unlocks: Other bexio users can authorize your app through Composio. No test-user allowlist, dev store, or unlisted-install mode is documented for bexio OAuth apps.
limits: No install cap, user cap, or restriction for unreviewed apps was found in the docs, changelog, or marketplace terms reviewed.
Per-minute rate limit applies per company; the numeric limit is not stated in the excerpt reviewed.
Confirm with bexio support before onboarding external users.
gates.time_to_reach: Not documented; expected to be the same as Gate 1 once the app exists

gates.name: Marketplace listing (partner track)
gates.unlocks: Listing in the bexio Marketplace so any bexio customer can find and install the app. This is a separate track from API access.
limits: Requires at least 10 bexio customers and at least 20 active users, plus a signed partner agreement.
Listing content in German, English, French and Italian.
Partner must provide first-line support to its own customers.
bexio may decline to activate or remove offers; no review criteria or timeline are published.
No annual fees or listing costs, but a 25% service fee applies on revenue from shared bexio users (20% for top 20% of partners).
gates.time_to_reach: Not published; bexio decides go-live timing at its discretion

steps.title: Get a bexio account
steps.detail: Sign in at bexio.com. If you do not have an account, sign up for a trial account. The developer portal uses the same bexio credentials.
gotchas: Test and development use may need a higher bexio plan; the partner agreement mentions a Pro+ account for Marketplace partners.

steps.title: Sign in to the Developer Portal and accept the terms
steps.detail: Open developer.bexio.com and sign in with your bexio credentials. Read and accept the terms and conditions, paying particular attention to the commercial-use rules in Section 4.4.
gotchas: Only community summaries of Section 4.4 were available. Read the full text yourself.
Section 4.4 may require you to inform bexio if you run your own business model on the API with at least five bexio accounts connected.

steps.title: Create a new app and set the Allowed redirect URL
steps.detail: Create a new app in the Developer Portal. Enter your product name and company URL. In the 'Allowed redirect URL' field, paste the callback URL from your Composio auth config exactly as shown.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Product name
values.value: Your app name. It must not contain 'bexio' or 'bx'.

gotchas: Redirect URLs must be defined when the app is created. Unknown URLs are refused and the user sees an error.
The URL must match the portal entry exactly, including scheme, host, path and trailing slash, or sign-in stops with an error.
Up to 10 redirect URLs can be defined per app if you need more than one environment.

steps.title: Add extra redirect URLs only if you need them
steps.detail: If you use a test environment or a second Composio project, add its callback URL as another allowed redirect URL, up to the limit of 10. Keep each URL exact so that no entry is mistyped.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The Composio catalog default is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Use the URL shown in your own Composio auth config, which takes precedence.

steps.title: Reveal and copy the Client ID and Client Secret
steps.detail: Open the app's 'App Details' section in the Developer Portal and reveal the Client ID and Client Secret. Store the secret in a password manager. Do not put it in front-end code or a browser app.
gotchas: The code exchange sends the client secret, so the app that performs it must run server-side.

steps.title: Create a custom OAuth2 auth config in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, create a custom OAUTH2 auth config for the bexio toolkit (slug: bexio). Paste the Client ID and Client Secret. Enter the authorization and token endpoints below. Check that the redirect URL shown there is the one you registered in step 3.

values.label: Scopes
values.value: Use the trimmed list from the scope step, not the 37-scope default.

gotchas: Composio reports no managed OAuth app for bexio, so this custom config is required.
PKCE: discovery lists S256 and plain, but the docs do not say whether bexio requires it. Test the flow first.

steps.title: Trim the scope list to what the app needs
steps.detail: Map each action your agent performs to the resource it touches, then request only those scopes. Use write scopes alone where you need write, because write includes read on the same resource. Keep offline_access only if you need a refresh token, and openid for the login identity.
gotchas: Scopes are fixed at authorization. Refreshing does not add scopes; adding one means every user repeats the full authorization.
The default 37-scope list shows every scope on the consent screen, which will look broad to users.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio using your own bexio account. Approve the consent screen, then confirm the connection shows as active. Make one read call and one write call that your agent needs, to check the scopes work.
gotchas: Access is limited by both the app's scopes and the user's bexio rights. If an action fails, check the user's role as well as the scope list.
Sign-in stops with an error if the redirect URL does not match the portal entry exactly.

steps.title: Plan refresh-token handling
steps.detail: Confirm that Composio refreshes the token before expiry and stores the new refresh token each time. Set an alert to renew the connection at least once a year.
gotchas: The refresh token does not expire, but the offline session closes if it is not renewed within one year.
Refresh-token rotation for new apps is not explicit. Use the refresh token returned on each refresh.

steps.title: Test with other users before wider release
steps.detail: Ask bexio support whether your app can be authorized by other companies before you onboard them. Then connect one test company account through Composio. Record any cap, warning screen, or rate-limit response you see.
gotchas: No documented test-user or install cap was found. Treat this as unconfirmed until bexio says so in writing.
Rate limits are per company per minute and return HTTP 429. Read the RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset headers and back off.

steps.title: Decide on a Marketplace listing (optional)
steps.detail: A Marketplace listing is separate from API access. If you want one, confirm you meet the requirements: at least 10 bexio customers, at least 20 active users, a defined target group, customer support, and a signed partner agreement. Then fill out the form linked from the partner page.
steps.est_time: 1-2 hours to prepare; review time not published
gotchas: bexio does not state a review timeline. It decides when offers go live and may decline or remove them.
No annual fees or listing costs, but a 25% service fee applies on revenue from shared bexio users.

steps.title: Prepare the listing content and support
steps.detail: Write the listing in German, English, French and Italian. Provide an optional video as a YouTube link. Set up first-line support for your end customers, because bexio refers customer questions about partner apps back to the provider.
gotchas: The app name must not include 'bexio' or 'bx', and the logo must not resemble bexio's.

steps.title: Sign the partner agreement and wait for go-live
steps.detail: After the form, bexio starts the partnership process. Review the partner agreement and the Marketplace T&Cs before signing. Wait for bexio to set the go-live date; it will tell you of planned appointments or deadlines.
gotchas: Either party may end the partnership with four months' notice, but not before six months after the start.
bexio may change the T&Cs; you are bound unless you object within 14 days of becoming aware of a change.
The partner agreement specimen is Version 0625 and may differ from a signed contract.

steps.title: Keep the app compliant after launch
steps.detail: Watch the API changelog for breaking changes. bexio gives four months' notice of critical changes and one month for other partner-relevant changes. If your app connects at least five bexio accounts through other services, declare this to bexio.
gotchas: bexio may restrict API access for misuse, overload or incorrect reporting, for the partner or for individual end customers.

Terms must be accepted; commercial-use rules in Section 4.4 apply.
The code exchange sends the client secret, so the app must run server-side.
Redirect URLs must be defined at app creation; up to 10 per app; unknown URLs are refused.
Renew at least every 12 months to keep the offline session open.
Adding a scope later requires every user to repeat the full authorization.
Per company per minute; HTTP 429 when exceeded. Numeric limit not stated in the excerpt reviewed.
At least 10 bexio customers and at least 20 active users for Marketplace partners.

requirements.item: OpenID Connect login and bexio API integration

requirements.detail: Required before a listing; specimen Version 0625 reviewed.
Partner must support its own customers.
Name must not include 'bexio' or 'bx'; logo must not resemble bexio's.

requirements.item: Declaration of five or more connected accounts
requirements.detail: Apps connecting at least five bexio accounts through other services must be declared to bexio.

scopes.effect: Identity scope. Keep it if you need the user's OIDC identity. bexio does not document a review tier for it.
Issues a refresh token that does not expire but closes if not renewed within one year.
Write access to accounting data; read is included.
Write includes read. Request contact_edit alone if you write contacts.
Invoice write includes read. Request only if your agent creates or edits invoices.
Payroll data is sensitive by nature. bexio does not publish a review tier, so expect scrutiny in any Marketplace review.
Allows payment changes. Request only if the agent must write payments; users will see it on consent.
Trim before connecting. Each one appears on the consent screen. The docs show no sensitive or restricted tier.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with an error after you click Allow, or sign-in stops
blockers.cause: The redirect URL is missing from the app's Allowed redirect URL list or does not match exactly.
blockers.fix: Copy the callback URL from your Composio auth config into the Developer Portal app, including scheme, host, path and trailing slash. Save and retry. Up to 10 URLs are allowed.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails or the client is rejected
blockers.cause: Client secret is missing or used from a browser or front-end app, or the wrong client ID was pasted. Probes show the authorization endpoint rejects unknown clients.
blockers.fix: Confirm the Client ID and Secret in App Details. Run the code exchange from your server, not from a browser.

blockers.symptom: Name or logo rejected for the Marketplace
blockers.cause: The partner name includes 'bexio' or 'bx', or the logo resembles bexio's.
blockers.fix: Choose a name without 'bexio' or 'bx' and a distinct logo before submitting the form.
blockers.contact: bexio Marketplace partner form (linked from the partner page)

blockers.symptom: Marketplace offer not activated or removed
blockers.cause: bexio decides go-live timing and may decline or remove offers that do not meet its standards. No criteria are published.
blockers.fix: Ask bexio in writing for the criteria and expected timeline before you invest in listing content. Plan for an open-ended wait.

blockers.cause: The per-company per-minute rate limit was reached. The numeric limit is not in the reviewed excerpt.
blockers.fix: Read RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset headers, and back off until the reset time. Confirm the limit with bexio.

blockers.symptom: Connection stops working after a long period
blockers.cause: The offline session closes if the refresh token is not renewed within one year.
blockers.fix: Refresh the token at least once a year and store the new refresh token each time.

blockers.symptom: Users see a consent screen with many scopes and may decline
blockers.cause: The Composio default list has 37 scopes and bexio shows all requested scopes on consent.
blockers.fix: Trim scopes to the ones your agent needs before connecting, and note that adding a scope later needs full re-authorization.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for bexio, so start with your own bexio Developer Portal app. Register the Composio callback URL shown in your auth config as an Allowed redirect URL, then enter the Client ID and Secret in a custom OAUTH2 auth config. Trim the 37-scope default before connecting, because bexio shows every requested scope on its consent screen.

evidence.claim: Composio has no managed OAuth for bexio, so the developer must register their own bexio app and supply client credentials.
evidence.quote: managed_oauth_available": false

evidence.claim: Published endpoints: authorization at https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio/protocol/openid-connect/auth, token at .../protocol/openid-connect/token, with userinfo and JWK endpoints under the same realm.
evidence.quote: Authorization endpoint https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio/protocol/openid-connect/auth

evidence.claim: Probing the authorization endpoint with an invalid client_id returned HTTP 400 and a login page saying the client was not found, so the endpoint is live and rejects unknown clients.
evidence.quote: Client nicht gefunden.

evidence.claim: The OIDC discovery document is live and lists PKCE code challenge methods 'plain' and 'S256'. The docs do not say whether PKCE is required for bexio apps.
evidence.quote: code_challenge_methods_supported": ["plain", "S256"]

evidence.claim: The offline_access scope issues a refresh token. The refresh token does not expire, but its offline session closes if it is not renewed within one year, so the token must be refreshed at least yearly.
evidence.quote: The returned refresh token will be valid indefinitely but the associated offline session will be closed if not renewed within 1 year.

evidence.claim: Read access comes with write access on the same resource, so an app that requests a write scope does not also need the read scope.
evidence.quote: Read access is granted automatically when a write scope is requested for a resource.

evidence.claim: Refreshing a token keeps the original scopes; any added scope requires the user to go through the full authorization again.
evidence.quote: Acquiring new scopes is only possible by going through the initial authorization process again.

evidence.claim: Access is limited twice: by the scopes the app holds and by the permissions of the user who set up the connection. Both must allow an action.
evidence.quote: The API access happens with the user rights of the user who set up the connection to the application.

evidence.claim: bexio publishes a scope table with read and write scopes per resource (for example accounting, contact_show/contact_edit, payroll_employee_show/payroll_employee_edit), plus OIDC scopes such as company_profile, email, offline_access and openid.
evidence.quote: accounting Write access to accounting data

evidence.claim: The API docs contain no tiering of sensitive or restricted scopes and no security-review step for scopes, so review impact by scope is not documented.

Rate limit: bexio caps requests per company per minute and returns HTTP 429 when the cap is hit, with RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset headers. The excerpt reviewed gives no number.
evidence.quote: The bexio API enforces a rate limit that limits the number of requests a company can make per minute.

evidence.claim: The bexio developer portal is live at developer.bexio.com; the fetch returned the title 'bexio Developer Portal' with no login wall, but no portal content (app form, terms, review rules) was visible in the fetch.
No install cap, user cap, or restriction for unreviewed apps appears in the API docs, the changelog reviewed, or the marketplace pages and terms reviewed.
evidence.quote: 2026-06-19 Required scopes updated for purchase bills, payment and expense endpoints.

evidence.claim: The identity provider moved from idp.bexio.com to auth.bexio.com (changelog entry dated 2024-10-01). Integrators who used the sub claim needed to switch to a UUID-based identifier.
evidence.quote: Changed IdP URL from https://idp.bexio.com to https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio

evidence.claim: Marketplace listing is a separate track from API access. bexio states that it does not restrict API access and that anyone can build an integration.
evidence.quote: We do not restrict API access: anyone can develop an integration with bexio.

evidence.claim: The marketplace partner page lists these requirements: at least 10 bexio customers and at least 20 active users, a defined target group, a user-friendly integration, multilingual support, customer support, and a signed partner agreement.
evidence.quote: At least 10 bexio customers (SMEs or fiduciaries) among your regular clientele.

evidence.claim: The same marketplace page requires integration through the bexio API together with OpenID Connect login for listed partners.
evidence.quote: Integration via bexio API and OpenID Connect login.

evidence.claim: Applying is done through a form linked from the partner page. The page says bexio will then get to know the solution and start the partnership process; no review timeline is stated.
evidence.quote: Simply fill out the form so that we can get to know your solution better

evidence.claim: The partner agreement page says there are no annual fees, membership dues, or listing costs, and bexio charges a 25% service fee on revenue from shared bexio users, reduced to 20% for the top 20% of partners.
evidence.quote: The partnership with bexio does not involve any annual fees, membership dues, or listing costs.

evidence.claim: Listing content must be supplied in German, English, French and Italian, with an optional video as a YouTube link. Partner offers may be in fewer languages, but the listing is shown in all four.

open_questions: No documented install cap, user cap, or unverified-app restriction for bexio OAuth apps was found. Confirm in the Developer Portal or with bexio support before onboarding other companies.
No review or verification step for OAuth apps (as opposed to Marketplace listings) is documented. The fetched Developer Portal page showed only its title, so its app form and terms were not visible.
Scope sensitivity classes (restricted or sensitive) are not documented; the scope table has no review tiers.
Marketplace review time and rejection criteria are not published. Only listing prerequisites, the form, and bexio's discretion over activation are documented.
The numeric per-minute rate limit is not stated in the reviewed docs excerpt.
Whether PKCE is required is not stated. Discovery advertises S256, but the docs describe a client-secret code exchange.
Full text of developer-portal terms Section 4.4 was not fetched; only community summaries were available.
Refresh-token rotation for new apps is not explicit. Migration notes say to replace refresh tokens with the ones returned on refresh.
The bexio Marketplace partner page returned HTTP 403 on the first probe but loaded on fetch. The partner agreement specimen is Version 0625 and may differ from a signed contract.
Composio's custom OAUTH2 config fields and exact callback URL for this project were not verified; use the URL shown in your own Composio auth config.
